slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: the interior angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.

Proof: in triangle ABC, draw the line through B parallel to AC (it exists and is unique by the Parallel Postulate). The angles at B on that line, from left to right, are equal to angle A and angle C as alternate interior angles, with angle B in the middle. Together they form a straight angle, 180 degrees.

Corollaries: the acute angles of a right triangle are complementary, and each angle of an equiangular triangle is 60 degrees.
